subtopic: Refraction through a Prism and Dispersion
stem:
A prism ABC (with BC as base) is placed in different orientations. A narrow beam of white light is incident on the prism as shown in the four option figures. In which of the following cases, after dispersion, the third colour from the top corresponds to the colour of the sky?

(Each option shows the same triangular prism ABC in a different orientation with a beam of white light striking one face.)

options.label: A
options.text: Prism with vertex A on the left and base BC vertical on the right (C top, B bottom); the beam strikes the upper slanting face AC and travels downward into the prism.

options.label: B
options.text: Prism with vertex A on the right and base BC vertical on the left (C top, B bottom); the beam strikes the vertical left face BC horizontally.

options.label: C
options.text: Prism inverted with apex A pointing down and base BC horizontal at the top (C top-left, B top-right); the beam strikes the left slanting face CA and travels downward into the prism.

options.label: D
options.text: Prism upright with apex A at the top and base BC horizontal at the bottom (B bottom-left, C bottom-right); the beam strikes the left slanting face AB and travels upward into the prism.

subtopic: Defects of Vision and Their Correction
stem:
Figures (1), (2), (3) and (4) respectively correspond to:

(Figure 1: an eye in which parallel rays from a distant object converge to a focus in front of the retina. Figure 2: the same eye with a concave (diverging) lens placed before it, so the rays now focus on the retina. Figure 3: an eye in which the rays converge to a focus behind the retina. Figure 4: the same eye with a convex (converging) lens placed before it, so the rays now focus on the retina.)

options.label: A
options.text: The short-sighted eye, the correction of short-sightedness, the long-sighted eye and the correction of long-sightedness

options.label: B
options.text: The long-sighted eye, the correction of short-sightedness, the short-sighted eye and the correction of long-sightedness

options.label: C
options.text: The short-sighted eye, the correction of long-sightedness, the long-sighted eye and the correction of short-sightedness

options.label: D
options.text: The long-sighted eye, the correction of long-sightedness, the short-sighted eye and the correction of short-sightedness

subtopic: Refraction through a Prism and Dispersion
stem:
A prism ABC (with BC as base) is placed in different orientations. A narrow beam of white light is incident on the prism as shown in the figures (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv). In which of the following cases, after dispersion, the third colour from the top corresponds to the colour of the sky?

(Figure (i): upright prism, apex A at top, base BC horizontal at the bottom, beam on the left face. Figure (ii): inverted prism, apex A at the bottom, base BC horizontal at the top, beam on the left face. Figure (iii): prism with apex A on the left, base BC vertical on the right, beam on the upper face. Figure (iv): prism with apex A on the right, base BC vertical on the left, beam on the left face.)

subtopic: Refraction through a Prism and Dispersion
stem:
Light is incident normally on face AB of a prism as shown in the figure. A liquid of refractive index \(\mu\) is placed on face AC of the prism. The prism is made of glass of refractive index \(\tfrac{3}{2}\). The limiting value of \(\mu\) for which total internal reflection takes place on face AC is

(The figure shows an equilateral prism with apex B at the bottom and the face AC horizontal at the top, with \(60^\circ\) angles marked at A and C; a layer of liquid rests on the top face AC, and the light beam enters normally through the slanting face AB at the bottom-left.)

subtopic: Refraction through a Prism and Dispersion
stem:
Two equilateral prisms are arranged as shown in the diagram, and two statements are given about them.

(The figure shows prism X upright with its apex pointing up on the left, and an identical prism Y inverted with its apex pointing down on the right; white light enters prism X from the lower-left.)

Statement 1: If white light is incident on prism X, then the ray of light which emerges out of the prism Y will be white light.
Statement 2: Prism Y recombines the seven colours.

options.label: A
options.text: Both Statements 1 and 2 are true but Statement 2 is not the correct explanation of Statement 1

options.label: B
options.text: Statement 1 is true but Statement 2 is false

options.label: C
options.text: Statement 1 is false but Statement 2 is true

options.label: D
options.text: Both Statements 1 and 2 are true and Statement 2 is the correct explanation of Statement 1

subtopic: Defects of Vision and Their Correction
stem:
Observe the given diagram carefully. What could be the causes of this defect?

(The figure shows an eye in which rays from a nearby object point A pass through the eye lens and converge to a focus behind the retina, i.e. the image is formed beyond the retina.)

1. The focal length of the eye lens is too long.
2. The eyeball becomes too small.
3. The focal length of the eye lens is too short.
4. The eyeball becomes too long.

subtopic: Refraction through a Prism and Dispersion
stem:
Study the following figure in which a student has marked the angle of incidence (\(\angle i\)), angle of refraction (\(\angle r\)), angle of emergence (\(\angle e\)), angle of prism (\(\angle A\)) and the angle of deviation (\(\angle D\)). The correctly marked angles are:

(The figure shows a triangular prism with apex angle A at the top. A ray enters the left face, with \(\angle i\) and \(\angle r\) marked at the first surface; the internal ray reaches the right face where \(\angle e\) is marked inside the prism and \(\angle D\) is marked at the second surface, while the extensions of the incident and emergent rays are shown dashed.)

subtopic: Refraction through a Prism and Dispersion
stem:

(The figure shows a triangular prism with apex angle A at the top. A ray enters the left face and \(\angle r\) is marked inside at the first surface; the internal ray reaches the right face and emerges with \(\angle e\) marked outside at the second surface; \(\angle D\) is marked at the point where the dashed extensions of the incident and emergent rays cross inside the prism. No angle of incidence is marked at the first surface.)

subtopic: Refraction through a Prism and Dispersion
stem:

A ray enters the left face with \(\angle i\) marked from the surface and \(\angle r\) marked inside; the internal ray reaches the right face where \(\angle e\) is marked from the surface, and \(\angle D\) is marked at the crossing of the dashed extensions of the incident and emergent rays.)

subtopic: Refraction through a Prism and Dispersion
stem:
Study the following ray diagram. In this diagram, the angle of incidence, the angle of emergence and the angle of deviation respectively have been represented by:

(In the figure a ray enters the prism through the right face — where p is the angle outside the surface and q the angle inside — travels across the prism, and emerges from the left face, where y is the angle inside and x the angle outside; z is the angle between the dashed extensions of the incident and emergent rays near the apex.)

subtopic: Refraction through a Prism and Dispersion
stem:
In the following diagram showing dispersion of white light by a glass prism, the colours P and Q respectively are:

(White light enters the prism and splits into a spectrum; the emergent ray Q is deviated less and lies nearer the original direction (shown dashed), while the emergent ray P is deviated more and lies farther below it.)
